title: API Design for AI Features — Expose the Job, Not the Vendor
key_insight: Design your API around the product job, such as extracting an invoice or drafting a reply. The server can change models behind that contract.
body:
## Expose the Job, Not the Vendor

A mobile client calls a provider-specific “chat completions” route even though the product feature is invoice extraction. Provider changes leak everywhere.

Design your API around the product job, such as extracting an invoice or drafting a reply. The server can change models behind that contract.

Return stable fields and explicit errors. Clients should not parse prose to discover whether the job succeeded.
common_mistakes: Clients should parse arbitrary prose as an API contract.
A retry should always create another paid job.
Model changes can never affect API behavior.
mini_exercise: Draw “Expose the Job, Not the Vendor” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: A stable product API hides model churn and gives clients clear states, errors, and versioned behavior.
explain_back_prompt: Use “Expose the Job, Not the Vendor” to explain API Design for AI Features plainly.
